identity: A single canonical hadith (Jarir ibn Abdillah's pledge of allegiance, Bukhari-type report). It has the standard two-part hadith form: a four-link isnad transmission chain (Musaddad > Yahya > Isma'il > Qays ibn Abi Hazim > Jarir ibn Abdillah), then the matn, Jarir's own reported words. Genre L in my doctrine. 34 tokens, one unbroken paragraph, zero <NL> tokens, no display list anywhere.
law: Isnad law (L1): the chain breaks after each transmission verb, asyndetically, and the break falls BEFORE qala, never after it, because qala is a speech verb and speech verbs OPEN a unit (E3). Each link, of the form 'qala + transmission verb + narrator (+ 'an X)', is one unit, and the boundary sits on the last token before the next qala. The short-tail brake (0b) is suspended in this genre: my recorded gold cut a 2-word link, and the four links here are perfectly parallel, which independently forces cuts (B2/E1). In the matn there is exactly one finite verb (baya'tu) and no second predication, so the matn is a single unit.
reasoning: Four sites, all decided by one rule: cut immediately before every qala. SITE i=1 (musaddad, before qala hadathana yahya). This is the verbatim positional twin of the only isnad gold I hold, doc_27a114d4e376 @1: hadathana Isma'il || qala haddathani Malik. There the boundary was also at index 1, also document-initial, also a 2-word link. The 2-word length does not protect it, because genre L suspends the short-tail rule, and that gold is itself the proof. hi. SITE i=6 (isma'il, before qala haddathani qays). Same construction one link deeper. I weighed the objection that 'an Isma'il and the following qala are semantically bound, since it is Isma'il who is speaking, so the cut severs a subject from its verb. But the recorded gold overrode exactly that linkage: there too the qala belonged to Isma'il, and gold still cut before it. The annotator segments on surface form at qala, not on semantic cohesion. L1 is stated as recurring, after EACH transmission verb; the four links are perfectly parallel; parallelism forces cuts (B2/E1); and cutting at 1 but not at 6 would be internally incoherent. hi. SITE i=17 (allah, closing 'an Jarir bin 'Abdillah, before qala baya'tu). The isnad-to-matn hinge, the strongest boundary a hadith has, and it obeys the same before-qala rule. Note the token is the second half of the personal name 'Abd Allah, not the divine name in isolation. hi. SITE i=33 (muslim). Final token, always a boundary by the format rule. hi. REJECTED CUTS. (a) After qala instead of before it (i=2, 7, 18): killed by the recorded gold, where qala stands on the right-hand side of the boundary at @1. (b) Treating the whole isnad as one unit and cutting only at the matn: killed by that same gold, which demonstrably breaks the chain internally. (c) Splitting the matn's coordinated verbal nouns, iqam al-salat / wa-itaa al-zakat / wa-al-nush li-kulli muslim. G2 does make coordinated masdars into units, but only when they carry heavy complements; the G2 items run 5 to 8 words, whereas these run 2, 2 and 3 words and are bare idafas with no predication, no subject and no PP frame of their own, all hanging off one preposition ('ala) governed by one finite verb (baya'tu). Section 0's conjunct-weight test sends bare nominals the other way, and this is the same shape as al-sam' wa-al-basar wa-al-shamm (no cuts) and al-'Iraq wa-Ustraliya (no cuts). Merge. (d) Cutting after the preposition 'ala (i=26) as a colon-in-disguise under H1/I2: rejected, since there is no cataphoric announcer, no <NL>, no display list and no MCQ stem; the complement is a short 7-word wa-chain riding inside a flowing predication, which is J5's shape, not H1's. (e) Splitting the eulogy salla allahu 'alayhi wa-sallam: no precedent, it is a lexicalized formula riding with the name it honours, and cutting it would strand 'ala iqam al-salat headless. Net: 4 boundaries in 34 tokens. My batch-1 prior is 7:1 under-segmentation, so I searched hardest for missed cuts; the only serious extra candidate was the matn list, and both the conjunct-weight test and the bare-noun precedents refuse it.
